utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So good morning, everybody. Good morning to you, Mr. Registrar. Could you kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, for the record all the accused are here. Prosecution it's Mr. McCloskey; Defence teams, I notice the absence of Ms. Tapuskovic, Mr. Nikolic, Mr. Bourgon, and Mr. -- no, Mr. Davis is here, my apologies to you, but with the columns in the way, sometimes it's difficult to see who is here and who is not. Thank you. I understand Mr. Zivanovic and Madam Fauveau would like to address the Chamber, preliminary. Yes, Ms. Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In fact, I would like to say exactly the same thing as my colleague, Zivanovic. Perhaps we should go into private session. It has to do with the motion filed by the Prosecution on Friday, confidential motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Let's go into private session for a very short while. I don't know why we should be in private session and why it was filed confidentiality, to be honest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we would simply like to inform this Trial Chamber that the Defence of Popovic, Beara, and Miletic support the motion filed by the Prosecutor because we feel that this would be beneficial for the accused as this is a very complex case. And as far as the Defence is concerned, we received an important number of documents disclosed to us by the Prosecutor; namely, regarding the Main Staff. And, for some of us at least, we do have some commitments right after the 20th of July, since at the outset, we had planned that the date would be the 20th of July. So if something is postponed, it should be after the legal holidays. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, on behalf of General Gvero, we were not going to raise the issue today, but we would invite some direction from the Trial Chamber as to which date we should respond. We have some specific submissions in relation to this particular issue, and, indeed, we will probably file a further motion in regard to matters pertaining to scheduling. So I would simply ask to some direction as to when that needs to be done by.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, I don't really think it should be very difficult for you to imagine or realise that it should be filed the earliest possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Well, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are a few days, basically, away from the deadline that we had imposed earlier, and what Mr. Haynes wrote in his reply yesterday as to the desirability of an earlier response from the Trial Chamber is, of course, it makes a lot of sense. And we have the intention of coming down with our decision or our response pretty soon. So I will consult with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Can I say we respectfully endorse what Mr. Haynes said. We simply want to know. If it's going to be 24 hours, it will be 24 hours. Forty-eight will be our preference, but we'll do it in 24, if need be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. By tomorrow noon, noon time.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Nothing, really, but would you lift the confidentiality of my response, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I assumed it was because of footnote 2, but I see no reason for the debate to be private rather than public.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. So we have lift the confidentiality, of your response, too. Borovcanin, I understand, have already replied but I haven't -- or not just me, because I asked my colleagues this morning. We haven't seen it as yet, it hasn't arrived to us, so that covers all the teams, no? One, two, three -- no, Nikolic. Nikolic, do you wish to state your position regarding this motion, Ms. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I will express the position of our team within the 24-hour limit, as we had planned to work throughout the summer in accordance with the previous instructions in view of the new disclosed material and also the witness we are expecting to see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. All right. So we'll try, assuming that you will respond by tomorrow noon, we will try to come down with our decision as soon as possible afterwards. We have other decisions in the pipeline, we have to look at them again. We'll deposit them in due course in the next couple of days. Other preliminaries? We hear none. Can we bring in Mr. Kosoric, please. Mr. Zivanovic and Mr. McCloskey and others, for that matter, do you think it's the case of giving him caution under Rule 90 or not? Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Mr. Kosoric.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm the Presiding Judge in this case. My name is Agius, and together with my colleagues, Judge Kwon, Judge Prost, and Judge Stole, we welcome you to this Tribunal. You're about to start giving evidence soon. Before you do so, our rules require that you make a solemn declaration tantamount to an undertaking to speak the truth during your testimony. The Usher next to you will hand to you now the text of the solemn declaration. Please read it out aloud and that will be your solemn undertaking with us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Please make yourself comfortable. You're going to be asked a series of questions by Mr. Zivanovic, who is appearing for accused Popovic here. He will then be followed, presumably, by the Prosecution, Mr. McCloskey, and maybe others. Before you start giving evidence, it is my duty to draw your attention to a special provision that we have in our rules of evidence and procedure by virtue of which you are entitled to object answering any question which, in your mind, could incriminate you. This, however, is not an absolute right. You can indicate your objection to the Trial Chamber, and then it's up to us to decide whether to accept your objection and exempt you from answering such questions or whether to compel you to answer the question not withstanding your objection. You have a further right, however, should we compel you to answer such incriminatory questions. Our rule, Rule 90(e) provides, specifically, that should this be the case, testimony compelled in this way by the Trial Chamber shall not be used as evidence in a subsequent Prosecution against you for any offence except if that offence is a false testimony, perjury. Have you understood my explanation to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And you do understand that coming here to answer questions from Mr. Zivanovic means also that you will need to answer questions from everybody else, including the Prosecution? You are aware of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. So having said that, we can proceed. Mr. Zivanovic, how long do you expect your examination-in-chief to last.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I believe that half an hour will be enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Let's go, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Kosoric. My name is a Zoran Zivanovic. I represent Vujadin Popovic in this case. I would like to ask you for the record to tell us your full name, first and last?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Svetozar Kosoric.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please also tell us how old you are and where you were born?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I was born on the 22nd of May, 1953, in the village of Kosece [phoen], municipality of Han Pijesak, in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Which schools have you attended and completed? Could you tell us that too?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: As far as military schools are concerned, I completed secondary military school for armoured vehicles, and also the military academy, also the department for armoured units.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you briefly --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know about the interpreters, but you're speaking too far from the microphone, and I try to follow you in your own language as well, but I can barely hear your voice. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kosoric, could you briefly tell us, please, what your career has been since you completed military academy, where you served?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Let me try and remember. After completion of secondary military school, I was working in Banja Luka in the educational centre for the training of units for about a year. After that, I completed the military academy and I then went to serve in Belgrade; more specifically, the Guards Brigade in Belgrade. I worked there for several years. Later on, I worked in the armoured regiment also in Belgrade, and I stayed in Belgrade until the 1990s, then I was redeployed to Valjevo. I spent about one year there, a year and a half, then I returned to Belgrade again to the same unit, that is, the Guards Brigade. In 1995, in mid-June, I was deployed to the Drina Corps in Bosnia-Herzegovina. That is where I remained until -- I can't remember exactly, but I think the beginning of 1997. Then I returned to Belgrade again, and that is where my service ended.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Where you pensioned off?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes, I retired.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Was a sickness the reason for your retirement?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes. In 1998, I retired and my illness was re-examined, and then I was re-employed in 1999. And in the year 2000, I was pensioned again.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You told us that in 1995, in mid-June, you were assigned to the Drina Corps. Could you tell us what position you held in the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: In the Drina Corps, I was assigned to the position of assistant Chief of Staff for intelligence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, while you were performing those duties who was your immediate superior?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: As I was assistant Chief of Staff for intelligence, my superior was the Chief of Staff of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: We are aware of the fact that at the time of your arrival that position was held by General Krstic?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: We also know that there is the term of management in the professional sense, could you tell us in that chain of command who were you subordinate to?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Along that professional line, I was subordinated to the chief of intelligence in the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And according to that professional chain of command, were you superior to the intelligence organs in the brigades?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember who was the intelligence officer in the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember. It was Nikolic, I just can't remember his first name. Nikolic, Momir, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: We know that shortly after your arrival an operation took place known as Krivaja 95, and in that operation the Army of Republika Srpska entered Srebrenica; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes, do I.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I won't go into the details of that operation itself, but I am interested in learning whether you remember that immediately after the Army of Republika Srpska entered Srebrenica, there were meetings between representatives of the Army of Republika Srpska on the one hand and representatives of the Dutch battalion that was stationed in Srebrenica, on the other, and that certain Muslim refugees attended those meetings?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember. At the time, I was a liaison officer between General Mladic and the Dutch battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember how many such meetings were held, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Two or three.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: What about the last meeting, regardless of the fact whether there were, in fact, two or three meetings? When was the last meeting held? Do you remember the time of day, for example, when the last meeting was held?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, it was held some time in the morning hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I will not be asking you anything in relation to that meeting specifically; in other words, anything about what about exactly went on during that meeting. I do want to know, however, whether prior to that meeting -- and we know where the meeting was held. Our information indicates that it was at the Fontana Hotel in Bratunac. Prior to that meeting, did you see Momir Nikolic and did you speak to him?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Each time there was a meeting, I would see Momir Nikolic about it, since he was providing the means for me to get to the DutchBat headquarters, and he would also provide an interpreter. I would then meet people from DutchBat and representatives from the Muslim authorities, whom I would then, in turn, take back to the hotel to speak to General Mladic there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I will now be quoting from a statement provided by Momir Nikolic, this is C1. It has been exhibited as C1. The relevant quote is in paragraph 4, as far as I remember. Shortly, you will be seeing the document on the screen in front of you; nevertheless, I will read it out loud for the benefit of the transcript. Do you see the text in front of you, sir? If that makes it any easier for you I can read it back to you.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: That will be fine, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It reads: "On the morning of the 12th of July, 1995, the forces of the Army of Republika Srpska, including components of the Bratunac Brigade, entered Potocari and took the town itself as well as the area surrounding the UN DutchBat compound. A third meeting was scheduled at the Fontana Hotel to be held at 10.00 with all the same participants. "On the morning of the 12th of July, prior to the above-mentioned meeting, outside the Fontana Hotel, I met" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt you, but on the monitor on the screen, initially we got an indication that you were reading from paragraph 2 --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 4, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly, this is why I am raising this because what the witness must have in front of him is paragraph 2 and not paragraph 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Maybe it is from my side interpretation or something --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no, I am not blaming. I'm just --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I know, I know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I am just pointing out that we have paragraph 2 and not paragraph 4. And that's why I couldn't follow you, actually, I mean, because I was reading paragraph 2, and I couldn't -- it didn't say what you were saying, although in part it did. So let's get paragraph 4, please, on the monitor.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'll read again, the second paragraph: "On the morning of the 12th of July, prior to the above-mentioned meeting, outside the Fontana Hotel, I met Lieutenant-Colonel Vujadin Popovic, chief of security of the Drina Corps and Lieutenant-Colonel Kosoric, chief of intelligence of the Drina Corps. On that occasion, Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic told me that all of the Muslim women and children in Potocari would be taken away from Potocari towards Muslim-held territory near Kladanj and that any men of military age among the crowd of Muslim civilians would be separated, temporarily detained in Bratunac, and killed shortly after that. I was told that it was my assignment to help coordinate and organise this operation. Lieutenant-Colonel Kosoric repeated this information after which we discussed appropriate locations for detaining and executing the Muslim men. I identified several specific locations: The old elementary school building, the Vuk Karadzic school (including its gym), the old building of the 'Djuro Pucar Stari' secondary school, as well as the hangar (which is 50 metres away from the old secondary school building). Lieutenant-Colonels Kosoric and Popovic spoke to me about the execution sites that would be used for the execution of these temporarily-detained Muslim men in Bratunac. We then specifically discussed two locations outside the town of Bratunac. These were the Ciglane state-owned company and the Sase mine in Sase town." Now, I would like to ask you a question about this quotation. Did you ever talk about anything like this to Momir Nikolic or did you tell him any of the things that I now read back to you?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I've been listening carefully, this sort of thing is never dealt with in this way. No conversation could have occurred outside the hotel, that would have been impossible. All I know is I was ordered something to the effect that we had nothing to do with the Muslim people, the captured soldiers. Rather, I was told that the civilian authorities and the Main Staff would be taking charge. I was also told that the units involved in Srebrenica, on that day or the following day, would be off to the Zepa enclave. What this document says is inaccurate. A decision must be taken at a higher level, at a meeting, this is not the sort of decision that is taken outside some hotel. This is hearsay, this is gossip, no more than that. This is no way for a military to go about resolving situations such as these.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I understand your answer. I would like you to be as specific as you possibly can in this regard. If need be, I will repeat this for your benefit. Did you ever tell him anything like this, under any conditions whatsoever? The document doesn't say that you ordered this. It simply reads that he was told. Did you tell him something to this effect?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: No, I never did. No conversation like this took place at all, not ever.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Another thing, in your presentation did Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic perhaps say anything like that, the same thing that I have just read back to you?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Kosoric. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zivanovic. Mr. Ostojic?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours. No questions at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I put, at this time --

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- in bold inverted commas, Mr. Ostojic. Thank you, Ms. Nikolic. Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, we have no questions at this time for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have no questions either, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: No questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: No, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All yours, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How long do you expect your cross-examination to last?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Several hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Hopefully shorter, but this has opened up quite an area, as I'm sure everyone understands.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Good morning. Are you -- what's your current rank, sir?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Lieutenant-colonel, retired.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Lieutenant-colonel, my name is Peter McCloskey. I represent the Prosecution. I will be asking you some questions on this. First of all, I'll quote you back, "This sort of thing is never dealt with this way." Sir, those words, let me ask you: Would this sort of thing be dealt with by General Mladic in the confines of a meeting room with his most senior staff before a decision, such as we've talked about here, was made?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: As far as I understand what you are saying, you misunderstood what I said. In order for any decision to be taken, there must be a meeting. Neither me nor Mr. Popovic nor, for that matter, Mr. Nikolic, were the persons who had the power to issue any orders or take decisions, even less out in the street outside our hotel. I fail to understand that. A decision had to be taken elsewhere and then conveyed to the commanders and not to us, the technical bodies that were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sir, listen to my question: Would such a decision, a serious decision like this, be made by General Mladic with his most senior staff inside a meeting room? Is that how such a decision would be made?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I don't know who took this decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, one moment. Yes, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It calls for speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No way, no way. Please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I please have the question repeated? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey, please, unless you wish us to read the question again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I can do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Would such a decision, a serious decision like this, be made by General Mladic with his most senior staff inside a meeting room? Is that how such a decision would be made?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Certainly, that is how a decision would be made, behind closed doors. Certainly not somewhere out in the open where people could then talk about it. It was possible that such a decision was taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, it's more than possible, isn't it, sir? You know what happened to the roughly 500 to a thousand men separated outside Potocari that day. They were all murdered, weren't this?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I don't know, I wasn't there. Were they killed, were they not killed, I don't know. Following those meetings, I left for Vlasenica; specifically, I went to the Vlasenica command, but I was following orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you go to Potocari on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I don't know specifically the date that occurred, but after one such meeting, we all went to Potocari, all those of us who attended that meeting. So, yes, I did go to Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So before going to Vlasenica you went to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I don't think I quite understand. I misheard you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, I'll help you. The meeting that Mr. Zivanovic was talking about took place in the Hotel Fontana on the morning of 12 July at 10.00 a.m. between General Mladic, civilian representatives of Bratunac, yourself, Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic, DutchBat, and Muslims. You remember that?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I do remember the meeting, but I don't remember Popovic being there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And where did you go after that meeting?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember that day, at that meeting, I left with a DutchBat officer for Kladanj. It had been agreed at the meeting that this officer would be monitoring the passage of the Muslim population to Kladanj. A corridor was to be made available to the population to use to leave the area. I've been thinking about this, and I think I spent that night in Vlasenica. The DutchBat officer stayed behind in this passage. That afternoon, a group crossed this area using this passage, a group consisting of women, children, and elderly persons. I may have been in Potocari on the morning of the 13th, but I can't say exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let me go back to the decision that we were talking about. You said it wouldn't be made outside with yourself and Momir Nikolic. Just to be clear, Mr. Zivanovic was not suggesting, nor was Mr. Nikolic suggesting in that statement he read, that the decision was made by you or Popovic. Tell us how once a decision is made, a serious decision like this is made, by General Mladic, in what command chain would this decision go through?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: What kind of decision my friend speak about because there is one decision that the witness answered that it is possible that the one decision was made?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zivanovic. I don't think it needs to be clarified, but if you could, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think talking about the decision you were referring to when you said: "This sort of thing is never dealt with in this way."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It's asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This is pure obstruction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Answer the question, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please repeat that question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey wants to know what would the chain of command spreading of or distribution of such decision be once it is taken? The question was: "Tell us once a decision is made, a serious decision like the one like this is made, by General Mladic, in what command chain would this decision go through until it reaches those that need to know it?"

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I personally believe that when a decision like that is taken at a meeting like that, the people who need to be there are the people who would then be implementing that decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And who would that be in the military organisation that you're familiar with?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: In my opinion, those summoned by the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And who would -- who would -- what branches would he naturally summon in order to do something that had to do with the transfer -- transportation and the detention of large number of Muslim prisoners?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I'm afraid I can't say. I was in charge of intelligence myself. That was my remit. I was never a member of the inner circle of the collegium nor, indeed, was I an assistant of the Chief of Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sir, you're a career -- you were a career JNA officer, you were a career VJ officer, you were brought to the VRS in mid-June 1995 for your expertise as a professional officer. So having your vast professionalism in mind, who would General Mladic want to carry out such a job? What branches would be dealing with the detention and transportation of prisoners?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, again it calls for speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's based on his experience. If he doesn't know, he will tell us he doesn't know. It's premised on the fact that he was an experienced JNA officer, a professional officer, and that he was placed where he was placed precisely because of this. So let's see. Do you want the question repeated, Mr. Kosoric, or are you still -- you still have it fresh in your mind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My area of work was intelligence. I never attended the staff command school or the national training school. Those were higher-level schools for higher-level command duties. The highest level that I reached was commander of a mechanised battalion. Those are tactical units. There is nothing else for me to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You haven't answered the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sir, can you answer my question?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Can you please repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Who would General Mladic normally have -- what branches of his military would he normally have to deal with the detention and the transportation of large numbers of prisoners?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I can't answer that question. You should ask him or someone at the same level.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If you give me his address, I'll go talk to him. As an intelligence officer, you would have been interested in interrogating Muslim army folks on the morning of 12 July, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes, but, as I said previously, General Krstic ordered for all units to go to the Zepa enclave. Therefore, we no longer had anything to do with Srebrenica or the population or, indeed, the Muslim soldiers. That was the reason I never interrogated a single prisoner.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So you must have been interested in those military men that were in Potocari in that group of people, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Of course I would have been interested in the line of duty, but, as I said, I was ordered to go to Vlasenica to track down the staff commander and to set up a forward command post towards Zepa. That was my task.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sir, you've already told us that you were in Potocari the day of that Hotel Fontana meeting, 12 July, amongst those military men. Surely you knew where those military-aged men were being held so you could interview them. Tell us about it.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: To be perfectly frank, I never spoke to a single Muslim soldier. I never spoke to any of the population there. I was only there when General Mladic was in Potocari and the group that left the hotel. Immediately after that I was off to Vlasenica in order to track down the staff commander who was then supposed to set up a forward command post near Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Who was the staff commander?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I don't know his name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't know any of the officers, I didn't know any of their names. Amovic, Acimovic, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: When did the troops of the VRS move towards Zepa?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Based on my recollection, and I might be wrong, the 12th or the 13th, one of those two days.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, sir, I don't think it's contested in this trial that the forces of the Drina Corps left for Zepa on the 13th of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, it is contested as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I don't think the question can be put in that form either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Why, Mr. Haynes?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Because, for one, my client has given very detailed evidence about his movements which involve him moving from Srebrenica, through Viogor, towards Zepa on the 12th. So to put the question in the form that that is not contested is wholly misleading to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, I think Mr. Haynes and Mr. Zivanovic are right. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think I can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You'll rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: -- rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It can easily be rephrased, but now you know what the position is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: -- testimony. You certainly know Mirko Trivic; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I don't know. Mirko?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: He's the commander of the Romanija Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Could you repeat the name once again, I didn't get it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mirko Trivic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, I'm not sure the witness understood, in full, your question because it was not noted in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Let me try again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sir, there is quite a bit of evidence in this case that the forces of the Drina Corps set off in the direction of Zepa and actually went to the Zepa area, the Krivace forward command post on the morning of 13 July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that is so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I think that's misleading. What does it mean "there is quite a bit of evidence in this case"? He should ask an open question, not put it in a misleading form.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, do you wish to comment or answer Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think it's a perfectly clear question that the person answered, the witness answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, let me consult with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, let's move on. But, you know, avoid such statements like "there is quite a bit of evidence" or "we know that." Mr. Kosoric, if you could answer the question, please. You have answered, actually. I think that is so. If you wish to add anything to your answer, then please, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sir, where were you on the morning of 13 July? This is the day after that Hotel Fontana meeting we spoke of that occurred on the 12th.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I am afraid I don't remember those details, but on the 13th, I went to Vlasenica to find the commander of the staff command - I think his name was Amovic - and to pass on the order that he should set up a command post in the village of Krivace, and when I got to Vlasenica, on the 13th, I did not go back.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And how did you travel from Bratunac to Vlasenica on the 13th?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: On the 13th I travelled, I think, in a Golf car.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And which road did you take?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I took the main road, Bratunac-Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So Bratunac-Kravica-Konjevic Polje-Milici-Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: At about what time did you set off from Bratunac on the 13th to do that?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I don't know, I really can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, don't worry about time. Morning, noon, or night? Morning, afternoon, or night?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I believe it was around noon, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And who ordered you to go?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I was ordered by General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Are you related to General Krstic?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes. He's my son-in-law [as interpreted], if that is a relationship.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You're married to his --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, one moment, because Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, translation is wrong, not son-in-law but brother-in-law.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Brother-in-law. All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sir, you're married to General Krstic's sister, I believe?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: No. My late sister is General Krstic's wife.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you for clarifying that. Now, where was General Krstic when he gave you the order to go to Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: In Bratunac, in the hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you see Colonel Beara in the area of Bratunac or Potocari those days?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I think I didn't. No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you see Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic in the area of Potocari or Bratunac those days?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: During the Srebrenica operation, Popovic was not present there, only General Krstic was there, the chief of the operations department - I think his name was Obrad, he's a Colonel - and the commander of the Signals Battalion, Jevdzevic, and myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You mean Obrad Vicic?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: When did you first see Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic in the Bratunac or Potocari area?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I saw him for the first time when Srebrenica was taken, that is, when the Serb forces entered Srebrenica. This was the 12th or the 13th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And where did you see him?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: In the hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: In fact, you were both staying at the Hotel Fontana; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I was throughout with General Krstic in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And you were -- you were staying at the Hotel Fontana at the time; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, for the first two days, I was at the forward command post. If my recollection is right, at Pribicevac - that is behind Zeleni Jadar - and after that, throughout, this could have been the 8th, I was at the hotel because I brought two transporters of the Dutch battalion and their soldiers. And upon orders, I put them up in the hotel, and that is where they stayed. They slept at the hotel. And I didn't go back to Pribicevac after that. I spent the entire time at the hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, we have information that General Krstic, because of his bad leg, was also staying at the hotel during this time-frame; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: No, he wasn't. I think that he spent the night at Pribicevac throughout, except when the operation was completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did Popovic spend the night at the hotel while you were there?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, you're familiar with the trial of General Krstic, I take it. You would have followed that trial as much as you could in the media when it occurred several years ago; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes, I followed it in the media.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you follow the trial of Colonel Blagojevic and Major Jokic that happened after that, the Srebrenica trial?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I did not. Only, if by chance, I would see it on television.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And how about this trial, it's been going on for some three years now, have you followed this trial?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: No, because there is not much reporting in the media about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Are you following it at all?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Not much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Where were you on 11 July when General Mladic and General Krstic walked through the town of Srebrenica on the late afternoon of 11 July?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I don't know if you understood me well. On the 8th, as far as I remember, on the 8th of July I arrived at the hotel, and from then on, I didn't see Krstic or General Mladic. I saw them again only that evening on the 11th at the hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Where did you have dinner that evening on the 11th?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Probably at the hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Where did General Krstic/General Mladic have dinner that evening?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I don't know, they are generals. After all, I'm only a lieutenant-colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Borovcanin told us that he saw them having dinner at the Hotel Fontana that evening. Surely if that's where you had dinner, you can have seen them, even though you're only a lieutenant-colonel?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: If I remember, I would have told you, because I've come here to tell the truth and nothing but the truth, so I don't remember. And I would have liked to have dinner with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, the first meeting at the Hotel Fontana happened at about 8.00 p.m., and you were -- you were at that meeting with General Mladic and the DutchBat people, Colonel Karremans?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I've already said, throughout that time I was a liaison officer between the Main Staff -- or, rather, the corps command and the forces in Potocari. I personally would bring, as well as Nikolic, representatives of the Dutch battalion, representatives of the Muslims, to the meeting at the hotel and take them back again to Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sir, my question was: You were at the meeting between General Mladic and the Dutch battalion folks. After you brought the Dutch guys there, that first meeting, you stayed; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And the second meeting, did you go into Potocari and help bring back the Dutch and the Muslim representative to the hotel?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you stay at the second meeting?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. I want to show you a short video-clip of that meeting, that second one and ask you a few questions about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And that should be Exhibit 2047. And this --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Before we start playing that, have you seen the video that's been out in public about that meeting for several years now?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I don't know until I see the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Have you seen any video of that second Hotel Fontana meeting?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay, well, let's see if this will help refresh your recollection.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Excuse me, Colonel. We're having a little trouble, that first one with them standing was the first meeting. This is the second meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: "I'm glad that we found Mr. Mandic. And what we have done in the short time tonight is putting ... put on a piece of paper the first general thoughts about the evacuation of the population. But also what are the first needs for the people. "If I may follow the list. I will start with what is from -- from the compound of Potocari and in the factories around the compound. We have now approximately between 15.000 and 20.000 persons. There are still persons coming in. We are accompanying them -- we are accompanying."

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you remember that pig being killed outside during the meeting?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, where is the information that it was a pig?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's been proved over the years, and it's a perfectly legitimate question. Mr. Mandic had testified it was a pig. He's heard a lot of pigs killed. I don't think that's an issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mandic didn't testify in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It doesn't matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but perhaps you can ask him what that was, if it wasn't a pig.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You're Bosnian, Colonel, do you know what that sound was?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I said I wasn't a colonel, I am a lieutenant-colonel. I do eat pork, but I find this rather funny. I don't believe they had pork to eat. I really find this a bit ridiculous. I am attending a trial, and I am in a courtroom for the first time, and I am astonished.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sir, it's the position of the Prosecution that General Mladic was intending to scare the Muslim representative, and by doing, so he had someone slaughter a pig outside the window. You were there. Did you hear that noise that we heard on the tape?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: This is ridiculous. First of all, this General Mladic would not -- such a thing would never occur to him. I have no comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There was another part to the question, whether you remember hearing those sounds.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. And I would have heard them for sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's carry on, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: "To find a place somewhere, to find a place somewhere. And we have between those refugees 88 wounded persons, of which four are very severe. And I heard from the Medecins Sans Frontieres" --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We are going to flip a little bit forward to save some time in the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What do you think General Mladic meant by those words, your people survive or vanish, talking about the salvation of his people?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I don't know what he meant. He said what he said, I have no comments to make. I am no expert to be able to assess his words and his views. He said what he said, and what he said was correct, was true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What was true about it?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: What he just said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Tell me, which part of what he said was true?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: What you just heard. You heard what he said. I don't understand what you're asking me. I'm not a psychologist or -- to assess the man to evaluate the man. I don't know why you are asking me this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's not a very good shot, but did you see yourself there at 01.40.43.2?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Looking at the screen, the person with his back turned, that is me. You can see the left part of my shoulder and my head, at least I think it's me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And just a couple of stills before, it showed quite a big mustache, so perhaps you could clarify that to make sure we are talking of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We will try to catch that distinctive feature. Ms. Stewart can ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think we can see your mustache.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Anyway, leave it. I could see it because I expected -- I anticipated what you're question was going to be, so I was looking.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think we can just finish this. It's practically done, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In this last part, the mustache was a bit clearer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: One last question: Sir, he says basically he wants the Muslim army to lay down their hands, and he says: "If you do that, you'll save your people from destruction." What did he mean by that?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I don't know. You're much more of an expert to assess that than I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's break time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's have a break, 25 minutes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, and I would like to call the counsel's attention to adjudicated fact number 183 regarding, that's 26th September, 2006, relating to the pig in the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And lieutenant-colonel and everyone, I hope to finish this -- this session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you go get the Muslim representatives, the morning of the 12th, and bring them to the Hotel Fontana meeting like you did the previous evening?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you see Momir Nikolic around the hotel that morning?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I think Momir Nikolic came with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And did you see Vujadin Popovic around the hotel, that morning of the 12th?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: No, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Were you at the meeting with him on the 12th?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I was at all the meetings when DutchBat representatives were there and Muslim representatives, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, were you with -- was Colonel Popovic at that meeting with that group on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: No, I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Didn't the Drina Corps security branch and the Drina Corps intelligence branches work closely together in your normal work sharing intelligence, security matters, prisoners of war, interviews, that sort of thing?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: The two branches were separate. They were entirely separate establishment-wise within the corps. Popovic was subordinated to the commander, he was assistant commander, and I was assistant Chief of Staff of intelligence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, the Trial Chamber, everyone is aware of that, but that wasn't my question. Can you answer my question?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Didn't -- in the normal course of your work, didn't you work closely with the security branch of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: We did not work closely together. We each did our own jobs, and then whenever there was information of interest to either of our branches we would exchange any such information.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So were you a close colleague of Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Not a close colleague. I first met him when I came to the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Well, we'll get into that a bit later. Now, let me show you a video-clip shot around the Hotel Fontana, the morning of the 12 July.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It should be Exhibit 2047.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. We've stopped it at 01.42.50.6.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And can you, starting from the left, from your left-hand screen -- yes, if you can -- better put your glasses on, can you -- do you recognise the people in this still?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: The one standing outside the door is Mladic's escort, and the one standing to his right is Popovic. I do not recognise the other two gentlemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay, and when you say "standing to his right," you mean the right of the picture as we see it. It's actually standing to the guys's left shoulder?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes, the one with a cigarette in his hand. That's Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And surely you know Radoslav Jankovic, Colonel, intel department.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: No, I was never in touch with that person.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, he was at the meeting -- both meetings on 11th of July, the previous meeting, sitting there next to General Mladic, or standing next to Mladic at the first meeting while Mladic was shouting at Colonel Karremans. Like you, he came over from the VJ in 1995.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I don't know Jankovic. There was a colonel there whom I didn't know, and we had no contacts, a professional or private.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And how about the fellow on the left side of the screen with his right hand in his pocket. Does that look like a nice profile of Momir Nikolic to you?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I don't think that's him. He had black hair. I don't think that is Momir Nikolic. He looks different, or else I've forgot.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's continue to play it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. That's -- that's clearly you with the --

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And everybody in this shot has a mustache, I guess. Who's the person that's got the back to the camera that you're looking at?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I don't know. The man over to the right, I think, is the DutchBat commander.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Over to the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So that's Colonel Karremans, the fellow with the white hair?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And could this be Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic that you're looking at or looking in the direction of, the fellow with his back to us?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Frankly, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's keep going.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's keep going.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I should for the record -- sorry, say that was -- Popovic was identified at screen number 01.42.55, and we can continue on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's -- there is two people whose faces we clearly see. There is a Dutch -- well, we see a Dutch soldier with glasses on. Do you remember Major Boering?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I don't remember any of their names.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, do you remember the major that -- I think he went out to Kladanj with you?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: No. I don't think I recognise him. The only person I recognise here is the commander with the mustache, grey hair.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Do you see yourself in this -- in this clip?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You're right over to the right of the screen?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: At 01.44.28 with your distinctive mustache.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's keep going.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's keep going and see if we can --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you see Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic there?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go back. Let's just take a look in the right-hand part of the screen. Well, let's go forward, I think he comes in again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see him now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's continue. Okay, thank you, 01.44.38, we see Popovic in the right-hand part of the screen with a mustache leaning over towards Mr. Mandic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We just saw you lean over and pick up a notebook. Have you had a chance to review any wartime notebooks before coming here to testify?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you keep your wartime notebook?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's keep going.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. What did you do with it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember. I didn't keep too many records at the time. I had the intelligence report that I had to submit to the Main Staff or another one to my subordinate units. That was the extent of the documentation that I was involved in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Have you had a chance to review any documents before coming here and testifying?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you make any effort to find any documents or any materials before coming here to testify?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: No. I did try to think back and remember all those developments.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you take notes as you were thinking back to help sort out your thoughts, like we all do sometimes?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: No. No. I do have a rough idea of what I do remember and what I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So what do you remember about the murders of the Muslim men?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I remember nothing at all about that because I wasn't there. I did not see any murders occur.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You spent in night in Bratunac on the night of the 12th; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Not the night between the 12th and the 13th. On the 12th, as far as I remember, I was on my way with that DutchBat officer to Kladanj, and I spent the night in Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, we've gone over that once, we'll go over it again a bit briefly. Let's just continue the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Lieutenant-colonel, we see then Mladic saying that - and referring to the words of the previous night - survival or disappear, and conditioning that on the laying down of the arms of the Muslim army. Now, on the 12th of July, the Muslim army, what did they do?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question, please? What they did, I don't understand what you mean by that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, did the Muslim army, on the 12th of July, make a breakout through the enclave area, from the area of Jablici [phoen], Susnjari, along the axis of Ravni Buljin-Konjevic Polje, towards Cerska?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And General Mladic knew that on the 12th of July, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: He should have known. I don't know whether he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And at what point, on the 12th of July, did you know that the Muslims were doing that, going in that direction, and not laying down their weapons?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I don't remember the exact time-line, but my assumption was that they would try to break out and escape towards Tuzla or Serbia. I said as much to the Chief of Staff, General Krstic. That was my assessment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So were you aware of General Mladic's reaction when he found out, on the 12th of July, that despite his three warnings of survive or disappear, the Muslim army did not lay down their arms, and they drove through the enclave. How did he react to that?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I don't know how he reacted. I don't know. I was not with him. The commanders who were with him probably knew. I was a mere assistant Chief of Staff in the corps. I did not attend any meetings where such decisions were taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What did you do when that meeting that we saw you at got out, the morning of the 12th of July, probably sometime 11.00 or so? What did you do? You must have thought about this.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. I just had to say my bit, and it wasn't my place to think about what the command and control section would be doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What was your bit, and who did you say it to?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: My opinion, which I shared with General Krstic, the Chief of Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what was that?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: That the Muslim armed forces would probably attempt to break through in the direction of Tuzla or else in the direction of Serbia; those who were refusing to surrender and lay down their weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And where did you get that intelligence information?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: That was my own assessment. I had been involved in intelligence work alone for about ten years, previously. It was my job to make assessments, such as those, and it was down to the commanders to decide whether they would lend any credence to my assessment or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Of course. But you would have relied on, in part, intelligence information you're receiving from people, say, Momir Nikolic, for example. He knew the area, he knew the terrain, so did you receive any information from Momir Nikolic that you passed on to General Krstic?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: This was my own assessment, specifically. There were no Muslim soldiers in Potocari and that was the reason I made that assessment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Were you with Momir Nikolic outside the Hotel Fontana after that meeting on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. He did share intelligence with me, though. He was one of my subordinates, according to the intelligence chain of command.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So we've heard testimony in this case from a Dutch major, Major Boering, who was at that meeting, and basically said that he went to Potocari and then realised there was lots of details he wasn't aware of, and he went back to Bratunac. And he says this on page 1976: "I then drove back to Bratunac and the Hotel Fontana, and I attempted to establish contact. After trying to find out some things, I ran into Major Nikolic, who said that everything had been agreed upon, that I should get lost, that there was no business of my mine here, that things had already started, and that I should leave immediately. He very clearly was not at all appreciating my return. "I then drove back and already saw that coaches were driving from Bratunac into the direction of Potocari." Question: "And was there any other VRS officer if you recall with Momir Nikolic when you saw him and he told you what you just explained to get lost?" The answer: "I believe that also the gentleman with the mustache, responsible for transport, was present there as well." Question: "Is that the one that you refer to as Kosovic or Kosoric?" Answer: "Yes, it is." So does that help you recall the, sort of, lost Dutch man coming back and asking Mr. Nikolic what they were to do and Mr. Nikolic sending him back to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I only know that before the buses I was off with an officer to Kladanj in order to make sure there was a safe passage. You should probably ask the officer who came to Kladanj with me, and he can confirm my response.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And that Dutch officer, did he walk on towards Kladanj after you reached that spot that we call Luke?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I'm happy to explain that because I actually remember that. When the two of us arrived, I'm not sure whether anyone else was there, we found the commander of the Vlasenac [phoen] Brigade, and another person who was probably his Chief of Staff. I spoke to both of them, conveying General Krstic's order. The order was as follows: Secure unhindered passage for all those wishing to go to Kladanj. I left that officer there and went back to Vlasenica myself to wash and to rest. Frankly, I really don't know what happened later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Prior to -- now, when you say "Vlasenica," where, actually, did you leave this officer? At the drop-off spot, at Luke, at the confrontation line, or somewhere in Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: No, I left him in Luke with the commander. I'm not sure if he was a chief or a commander. He was a representative of that brigade command, and that's where I left the officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And where did you go after resting?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I left for Vlasenica to wash and to rest. The morning on the 13th, I was expected back in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, before going to Luke with this Dutch officer, did you go to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I did go to Potocari one of those days, I can't remember which exactly. Mladic was there as well and all those who attended the meeting at the hotel was off to Potocari, but I can't remember whether it was the 12th or the 13th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And were Muslims getting on buses when you were there?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: No, they weren't. I didn't see Muslims. I did see Muslims in Potocari, and I saw soldiers of the Dutch battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you see vehicles, buses, trucks?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, there were some buses and trucks, but I didn't see people boarding them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Were there military-age men in that crowd of Muslims?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: To be quite frank, I don't know. It was a large group of people, men, women, children, old and young, I don't remember. There were all kinds there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Were you interested that some of them could have been officers from the 28th Division with valuable information right there in your hands?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I didn't show an interest because the order had already reached us that we were to go to the Zepa enclave and that this was going to be taken over by other organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What was going to be taken over by other organs?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: The civilian authorities and as far as the military is concerned, that the Drina Corps had nothing to do with it, that it was the business of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What was? What was the business of the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: The entire organisation of security and protection of the population in the territory of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Were you aware that able-bodied men were being separated from their families while you were in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I am not aware of such case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Were you aware at any time on the 12th or 13th of July that able-bodied Muslim men were separated from their families in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I am not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Were you aware on 12th of July that hundreds of able-bodied Muslim men were separated from Potocari, detained in at least one small unfinished house in Potocari, and then transported to a hangar near schools in Bratunac for the night of 12 July?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I am not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you hear what happened to some of these men on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you or the Drina Corps make any effort to feed any able-bodied men from Potocari?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I don't know who engaged in any such activities. I didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's play a video-clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: See if this helps refresh your recollection.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It should be Exhibit 2047. And we're starting at 02.04.18.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And surely you recognise General Krstic in this shot.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And as you'll see, he's giving an interview to the press. So let's watch this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you see yourself there?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And that's at 02.04.26. We see buses behind you. We also see a white-haired man behind you. Do you remember standing around while officers are giving interviews to the press?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What you are doing there?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I have already said that after the meeting with Mladic at the hotel and with representatives of the Dutch battalion and the Muslims, all of us went to Potocari because Mladic wanted to address the people of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So what were you doing there?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I've already answered your question. We -- all of us went there. Mladic said that we should all go to Potocari for him to address the people of Srebrenica. I couldn't avoid it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So were you doing any intelligence work?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You were just part of Mladic's entourage?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And you did nothing else?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And how long did you stay in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember from this distance, 15-20 minutes, maybe half an hour, roughly for as long as Mladic stayed there; that is, the same amount of time that I and all the others in the group stayed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Was this before or after you took your trip to Luke with the Dutch officer?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: This could only have happened before that. Because immediately after that, I left with the Dutch officer to Luke.
