utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So part of your job of going all the way to Luke was helping organise the route that the evacuation would take?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: My task was to go to Luke and to pass on the order that the path should be made free for the passage of the persons from Srebrenica, those who wished to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So clearly your job in helping to assist the transportation route would have started in Potocari so you could get an idea of the number of people that would be moved, the kinds of vehicles that would be moving them, fuel, other things that might help this job happen; right? It didn't just you would begin -- or did it just suddenly begin with you just driving to Luke?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: You didn't understand what I was saying. I had nothing to do with the organisation, the transportation, and the rest. My only task was to go with the DutchBat officer to Luke and to ensure free passage. As for the route and everything else, I had absolutely nothing to do with it because it is not within the purview of my intelligence work. I strictly adhered to my responsibilities. Transportation, logistics, food, that is the responsibility of other organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: But you'll agree that aside from General Mladic and, I believe, Colonel Jankovic, you were the only one who was at all three meetings who helped organise all this. So you would have had more knowledge about this than anyone?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I keep telling you what it is that I was doing, but you're refusing to understand me. My job was the job of liaison officer. I was a liaison officer. My task was to go from the hotel to Potocari, and from Potocari to the hotel. As for others, Jankovic and the others, I don't even know Jankovic. I had nothing to do with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's continue with the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Also the site.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: -- concerned about. Good memory, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's proceed. We are going to show it, but not broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. You can see that they only got one part of the conversation, and, as you can see, it -- the persons asking "is it Cica?" And it makes a reference to a Pop, or Popa. What was the nickname for Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Popovic or Pop, that's how we called him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. On July 9th, were you with Momir Nikolic in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Whether I was there on the 9th, I'm not sure, but I told you that probably from the 8th until the 12th, I was continuously in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you get any Muslim prisoners during that time?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did the army?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm unable to tell you that. If anyone knows, then it should be Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, you were still an intelligence officer.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was, but I'm assistant Chief of Staff of -- in the corps. I cannot know how many prisoners they may have had in seven or eight brigades. I would just receive written reports from them or intelligence reports. I didn't have time to tour all the brigades and to talk to all the prisoners. Those conversations were conducted by the organs in the brigade and not me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, had there been -- had there been prisoners on July 9th when heavy fighting was going on, I'm sure you'll agree with me that Vinko Pandurevic's troops were involved in fighting, you would have wanted intelligence from prisoners to be able to send down to the various brigade units, such as the kind of information you may get from a prisoner; the location of the enemy forces, the strength of the enemy forces. So, surely, you would have remembered had you had prisoners and received that kind of important intelligence. You were the man that was right there by your own words.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was right there, but I didn't speak to them personally, and I didn't know that they had prisoners at the level of the tactical group or battalion companies. They interviewed people and gave assessments and passed them on to the superior command. In those days, I didn't speak to a single captured Muslim soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, that wasn't my question. Did you receive intelligence from captured soldiers on the 8th, 9th, that time-period. It would have come up the chain to you. Did you receive that intelligence?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: It didn't come to me personally. It could only come in if you sent it in encrypted form to my deputy who was in Vlasenica, because throughout that period I couldn't read intelligence reports as I was in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You didn't get intelligence in the field? You're at the forward command post and you're not reading any intelligence reports or getting any intelligence; is that what you're telling this Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I'm saying. I didn't read them. I said, and I say it again, I was not at the forward command post from the 7th to the 11th. I returned to Bratunac and I was at the hotel, and I say that with full responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And you didn't receive any -- well, I'll just leave it at that. When did General Krstic become commander of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, he officially took over the corps in the second half of July. That was when there was the take-over of duty between him and the previous commander. Maybe the 21st -- or, I don't know exactly, within a period of two or three days around that date.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, surely you would have heard of the small ceremony that occurred on the evening of 13 July in Vlasenica where General Mladic assembled the officers there, including Major Golic, who has told the OTP about this, where Mladic told the assembled group that now General Krstic was the commander of the corps and General Zivanovic was no longer a commander. Certainly you would have known that; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know that. I heard of that. But this was just an oral order, but the official take-over of duty between the old and new commander took place when I just said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, Mladic's oral order is a binding order; isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes, but a written order is a written order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So General Krstic was the commander on the evening of 13 July after Mladic had that ceremony and did what he did; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: That was an oral order, but in an army, what becomes official is once the documents are signed and the duty is officially handed over and taken over. It is from that moment that you become a commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What do you know about the 10th Sabotage Detachment?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: The 10th Sabotage Detachment was a detachment of the Main Staff of the VRS. Do I need to say anything more?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Whatever else you know about it.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I don't know anything in particular about them. I know their commander because he worked in the same unit in Belgrade as I did. Now, what activities they engaged in, I don't know. He was subordinated to the Main Staff, and they worked for the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, they had a specific intel function too, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Probably they worked for their superior. They had no contact with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: But they had an intel function, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: They must have had, but they didn't cooperate with me. They submitted their reports to the Main Staff and their own superior.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And who was that?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: The chief of the intelligence administration was Colonel Salapura.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you see Colonel Salapura in Bratunac when he was there?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I did not, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And have you been to the 10th Sabotage Unit headquarters outside of Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I didn't quite understand what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Where was the 10th Sabotage Detachment located?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: As far as I can recollect, their command was in Bijeljina. That's what I think, at least, but I don't know for sure. And they had a post near Tisce, several houses where they stayed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And were you -- did you visit there near their place near Tisce?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I didn't visit them, but I know roughly where they were. I had no need to visit them. They were not subordinated to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to an exhibit, number 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I'm going to play you portions of this video and ask you some questions. We see that it starts out in the Cyrillic. That gives the date of the intercept -- or excuse me, of the video, as 14 October, 1995. And it's the first anniversary of Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you remember going to this ceremony of their -- of October 1995?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you go?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did Popovic go?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Now, who was there I can't remember. I see here in the clip Krstic, and we went there on the occasion of their anniversary, and they carried out a drill to demonstrate the work of their unit, and we were invited as guests.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Why would the chief of Drina Corps intel go to a Main Staff function like this?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: This is not the Main Staff. This is a unit that was demonstrating a drill in Vlasenica. They were demonstrating their weapons, their combat abilities, climbing up and down a building, and that is why it was interesting. And the corps command was in Vlasenica, so we went there as guests, we were invited to go there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, let's take had a look at this and maybe you can help determine where this is. I don't think it's in Vlasenica, not in the city, anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay, we just heard the name Erdemovic, Drazen. You must recall when he was arrested in Serbia in a 1996 and very publically was shipped to The Hague and confessed to his unit and himself taking part in the summary execution of some 1200 people on July 16th, 1995, a few months before he got an award here at this ceremony. Do you remember all that news in Belgrade at the time?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So in October of 1995 you were surely aware, as the chief of intelligence of the Drina Corps, that this unit, the 10th Sabotage Unit, had been involved in murdering prisoners in the Zvornik Brigade area; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I don't know where they operated.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you answer my question. Were you aware of the murders they comitted near Pilica?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I know nothing about that. All I know is based on media coverage. All I know is what was actually recorded in the media and on TV.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise yourself standing there?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's continue it, briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you recognise the person over your left shoulder in this picture?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And who is that, for the record?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The accused in this case?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps not. I don't know. Now that I've had a closer look, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, let's play it. Take a good look.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I don't know about the previous image, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So, at this anniversary function, was there any discussions at all of the 10th Sabotage murdering people?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Not that I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, I want to talk to you a little bit about Zepa, though, I don't think we need to go through the whole -- the whole film. There is a longer film, but I don't think we need to play it all. One more question: Does that just -- seeing these woods and this house, does that refresh your recollection of where, actually, you were that day?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I can't remember specifically. I do remember some certain sections. There was a drill going on at Loznica [as interpreted], special units climbing house roofs. This was probably outside Vlasenica, and they were training soldiers about all sorts of technical information and then weapon details, different kinds of weapons. I'm not sure. This was outside any settled area, and obviously this was a place where -- that they chose to show these soldiers how these weapons were used.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. So is this in a little village not far from Vlasenica where the 10th Sabotage that barracks? Sir, did you get a translation of my question?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't understand the question. I said this was somewhere outside where they did some shooting practice, and they used various weapons, but I don't know where exactly. It's certainly outside Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, Zepa. You were General Krstic's intel officer for Zepa; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: It might be advisable if the Trial Chamber check with the witness whether he spoke -- understands English and invite him to take his headphones off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey. Do you -- before I ask the witness the question, do you have any information?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, I don't, but I think it -- it might --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Kosoric, do you understand English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Nothing at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nothing at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Can you remove your headphones for a while, please. Yes, Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Your Honours, our submission is that the Prosecution should not be permitted to ask the witness any questions about this particular topic. The witness has been brought here under an unusual and quite rare procedure. He's come here to give evidence in response to the testimony of Momir Nikolic. Momir Nikolic was called, as I, of course, don't need to remind you, as a witness of the Trial Chamber. Thereafter, the Defence for Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic sought leave to add this particular gentleman to their 65 ter list, and the reality is the only reason they did that and the only reason they were allowed to do that was to respond to the fairly narrow issues that arose in relation to Nikolic's evidence. Now, Your Honours, we have not objected to the broadening of the questions that my learned friend has asked for a number of reasons, but primarily because he has stuck within the remit of Srebrenica and Potocari. And it's certainly arguable that that's relevant to what Momir Nikolic had to say, but Momir Nikolic gave no evidence at all in relation to Zepa. And in our submission, the fact that this witness has been called in response to Miomir Nikolic's evidence is not a green light for the Prosecution to ask him about absolutely every aspect of the case, and in particular about Zepa. And we contend that this particular procedure needs to be kept within very close and narrow bounds, and if the Trial Chamber allows my learned friend to ask the witness about Zepa, it's far outside the boundaries of what should be permitted, particularly, if I could end where I begun, bearing in mind the unusual and rare procedure that brought him here in the first place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Josse. Mr. McCloskey, would you like to comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. First of all, you would say there is nothing unusual or rare about this procedure. It's a perfectly normal, appropriate part of this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Skip that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And this was brought as a Defence witness in a case where joint criminal enterprise to move out the populations of Srebrenica and Zepa is charged. As Directive 7 reminds us, Srebrenica and Zepa, basically, the Muslims of Eastern Bosnia. We have the chief of the Drina Corps intelligence, who we see was intimately involved in the first joint criminal enterprise -- the first part of the joint criminal enterprise, setting out the roadway, by his own words, upon which the Muslims were being move out. To call a witness of this calibre, of this high rank, and to limit his testimony to only part of the joint criminal enterprise that he played such a crucial role in would be doing a disservice to the trier of fact. I -- as you can see, I've said I'm not intending to spend a lot of time in Zepa, but he's also tended to try to distance himself from Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic, and I have some video of him and Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic together that I think is important to show you that the distance that he's talking about is -- is not accurate. So on those two grounds, I would like some time to go there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Let me consult with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is a decision, a majority decision, Judge Kwon disagreeing. We are of the opinion and conclude that since what you have explained does relate also to the credibility of witness and consider also that subparagraph (ii) of paragraph (h) of Rule 90 does allow cross-examination to expand on where the witness is able to give evidence relevant to the case for the cross-examining party. Due to the subject matter of the case, we are allowing the question. However, we are also in agreement that considering this late stage of the proceedings, we are -- we conclude that you should limit -- use your discretion and limit your question to the bearest possible and not expand as much as you would like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just for -- not in agreement, it should not have been allowed at all given the late stage of the trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So that's clear to you now, so let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'd like to show you a video. It's Exhibit 4567, and it's dated, we believe, 22 August 1995. We think it's near Borike, and it should have you together again with Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic. And given your answers -- excuse me, 4568, and it's not Borike it should be area of -- perhaps the area of Gorazde. And I just want to ask you about what you're doing with Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you recognise that area, 22 August? Very distinctive bridge and river.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I don't quite remember this. I don't have this very image in my head. I don't remember the location. If I look again ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's see it again, maybe he remembers now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This could be Rogatica, possibly. There is this young man with the apple, and he hails from Rogatica, but I can't really tell you when we were there and what exactly we were doing. It was probably a lunch that we had there or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Were you doing military work together?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: No, we each did our own work.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So you were doing nothing together aside from having lunch?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Certainly not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What's the comment about war criminals about?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I have no idea. I really don't remember. I don't remember this footage, and I don't remember the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Who was the -- what's the name of the guy with the apple?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: His name is Zoran, Zoran Carkic. I think so, unless I've forgotten.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what was his position?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: He was with the Rogatica Brigade, assistant commander for security and intelligence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So in thinking about it now, you're with two security officers. Do you have any memory of what you were doing?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: The first thing you have to understand is the Zoran appearing here is assistant commander for security. He's Popovic's subordinate in terms of his technical duties. He's also an assistant for intelligence, which makes him subordinate to me. It was probably in the same day that both Popovic and I chanced to simply be with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, taking you into Zepa, you were -- were you General Krstic's intel officer for the Zepa operation?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And we have evidence from the brigade commander who you don't remember, Mirko Trivic. In his notebook of Zepa, it says on the 23rd that: "Leave part of the forces at Bezimeni, Vis, under Strmica and attack forces in the sector," and then it says, "task: Purtici village! Deadline until 1400 hours to bring the forces to the bridgehead." First of all, can you tell us what a bridgehead is in this context?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I can't explain anything about our own forces. I was an intelligence officer, and I don't know what assignments exactly the units were given. It wasn't my job.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sir, my question was purely what does the term "bridgehead" mean?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know how he issued that assignment, and I understood nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What is a bridgehead?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He told you he doesn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think he's telling me he doesn't know what the assignment was, I'm just asking him the word.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Why don't you find the word in B/C/S in the original document and put to him that particular -- that exact word and see whether it has been translated correctly in the first place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. That's a good idea. I can hand the witness the handwritten --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any objection from -- Mr. Zivanovic? None. So Usher, please, if you could assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Lieutenant-Colonel, I am just looking for the meaning of this word, and you'll see it's the last word --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can we see it on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: For the record, this is P04309, page 48.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, it's the last part that your attention is being drawn to. Can you explain what you understand by that, please, especially the last word?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He probably meant for new forces to be introduced. That was probably what he had in mind. This is such shorthand, such artist shorthand that I fail to understand what it means.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sir, what's that last word with the exclamation point next to it? Can you just read it out in your language?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Bridge railing. It could be a bridge. It's simply not clear. I'm not sure what I should answer. If I knew, I'd be glad to provide a response, but it's probably about introduction of new forces into that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could we just get from the translator what he is saying in Serbian, what is that last word?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you say that last word all by itself, just slowly and clearly?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Purtici village, dead-line by 1400 hours for forces to be introduced to the bridgehead or the bridge railing. It was probably a river there or a stream there that was taken and then new forces needed introducing into the area, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: One more try, can you just tell me the last word, just the last word, and just say it clearly in your language.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And, please, interpreters, we don't need the English.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay, and interpreter could you repeat that for us, in Serbian?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Mostobran." I read that, didn't I? But we don't use the word. We have --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay, "mostobran." What is a "mostobran"?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Do you recall in the last part of July and early part of August, hundreds of Muslims from Zepa and Srebrenica fleeing across the Drina river and going over and seeking refuge in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I know that after the fall of Srebrenica most of the Muslim soldiers crossed to Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And we have intercepts in this case where General Krstic mentioned you and Popovic going over to Serbia to get those prisoners. Were you involved in that?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And were you able to get the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I don't know the answer to that question. Serbia simply did not wish to deliver them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And how did General Krstic react to that?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I have no idea. How could I know what his reaction was. They -- we were just told that they would be staying where they were and that was the end of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Were you ever made a commander of a small unit on the 25th of October with Colonel -- Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic as your Chief of Staff in charge of chasing down leftover Muslim groups from Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let me show you a document, 65 ter 4574. And this is really the last document I've got.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we could just show it to the witness, maybe it will help refresh his recollection.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let me give you the hard copy, it's always easier, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Put it on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just take a little time to look at this. There is an actual hard copy, if you think that's easier than having to squint at the computer. And this is no --

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: It's easier on the computer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Fair enough. We see from this that we have something described as an order in the name of General Krstic entitled "Searching and Control of the Terrain," and it talks about the latest data suggests that in the territory of Srebrenica enclave and it goes on. I'll leave you alone for a minute so that you can look at it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: When you are ready, Mr. Kosoric, tell us, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This order, as can be seen, was written but it was never implemented nor was any search carried out. It was just put on paper, but what it says was never carried out nor was the terrain searched. That's as much as I can say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So do you remember this order being created?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what happened to it?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: It was not implemented for unknown reasons. I don't know what the reasons were. We probably didn't have the forces to do it. We didn't have the strength, because if we had carried it out, I would remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: But were you consulted on this order as it was being drafted? Surely you weren't put in command over Vujadin Popovic without it being discussed first?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I am convinced that this was written without any consultations. I see that the order is written, but such a unit was never formed nor was anything done pursuant to this order. I said -- think we should perhaps ask the others, but I am a hundred per cent sure that none of this was done.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That was wasn't my question.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Please, go ahead. Ask me. Ask me the question again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You said you remember this order; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Now that I see it, I remember, otherwise I wouldn't remember it. Did you understand what I was saying? This order was never implemented. It's just there, that letter on paper. The unit was not formed. No search was carried out because that is something I would certainly remember because it's indicated here that I was the commander, and there are many orders that were written out that were not implemented because of certain reasons that may have occurred at the level of control and command.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So you never discussed this order with Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: If we had implemented it, we would have discussed it. Is it clear what I am saying? It was not implemented, ever, at least I do not remember. Ask him, perhaps he can remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Shall we have the break? How much longer do you have?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm finished, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Oh, you're finished. Then just a moment of consultation, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you have a re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Not yet, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Two or three minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: With your indulgence, we have some questions for the witness, after which we'll be finished. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Kosoric --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: About two or three minutes of procedural matters after the witness is finished as well, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I am sure there will be no objection. Thank you. We were going to come to you, in any case, on procedural matters. Judge Kwon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Kosoric, there are some parts that are unclear to me in your answers given to the question put by Mr. Zivanovic, Defence counsel for Mr. Popovic. Do you remember that Mr. Zivanovic read to you the parts of Mr. Momir Nikolic's statement referring to the separating able-bodied men from the crowd and killing them later on?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I remember what he read out to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And I read out to you your answers to that question: "I've been listening carefully. This sort of thing is never dealt with in this way. No conversation could have occurred outside the hotel. That would have been impossible. All I know is I was ordered something to the effect that we had nothing to do with the Muslim people, the captured soldiers. Rather, I was told that civilian authorities in the Main Staff would be taking charge." What do you mean by the civilian authorities in the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: When I said "civilian authorities and the Main Staff," I meant that everything that was happening in the territory of Srebrenica would be taken over by them, and the units who took part in Srebrenica operation would move on to the Zepa enclave, so that the Drina Corps and the Drina organs had nothing more to do with the Srebrenica enclave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So you said "civilian authorities and the Main Staff," not civilian authorities in the Main Staff. Very well then. Next part of your answer was like this: "What this document says is inaccurate. A decision must be taken at a higher level, at a meeting, this is not the sort of decision that is taken outside some hotel. This is hearsay, this is gossip, no more than that." So I'm interested in the word "gossip." What kind of gossip are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I primarily refer to what Nikolic said, that we were consulting in front of the hotel. In my view, that is absolutely unacceptable. In military life that is not possible. This can just be rumors, chatting, it's not a meeting. It's not -- what happens in front of a hotel is just you go out to have a cigarette when you -- when we left the meeting. So it was not possible for us to make a decision like me, Popovic, or Nikolic. Who are we to make any decisions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Nobody -- Mr. Kosoric, nobody at this courtroom are saying that you made that decision at the time. What gossip, what rumors did you hear at the time?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: We didn't hear any rumors nor was this discussed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I have -- but let's go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Can you remove your headphones again, please. Thank you. Yes, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it's about the answer given to the question posed by Judge Kwon. It's line 1 to 3, page 10 [as interpreted]. What the witness said is that the rumor was what Momir Nikolic said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What you do you mean page 10?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [In English] Seventy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And which line?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Seventy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but which line?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [In English] 1 to 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, 1 to 3. Okay, I understood better now.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What the witness said is that the rumor was about what Momir Nikolic said, and in the transcript, what we should have read is: This is what was rumors. And then he said that -- well, he carried on about the cigarettes and what happened in front of the hotel. Could we have clarifications about that because he was talking about rumors in front of the hotel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Judge Kwon, would you like to go through? I think I can understand as well. To be honest with you, I don't think further questions need to be put. In my mind, it's clear what he means and what he's said. But I've asked Judge Kwon because it was an answer to his question, so if you wish to proceed further with it. Okay. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm sure we can take the audio and get a proper translation. I think that's the problem that we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. But in any case, it's -- I'm talking about the gist of the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's leave it then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Mr. Kosoric --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Microphone -- the headphones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Headphones. We've come to the end of your testimony. You're free to go back to where you come from. On behalf of the Trial Chamber, I wish to thank you for having come over and given testimony; and on behalf of everyone, I wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Mr. Josse, we are in agreement we can stay a further five minutes, no? I can't see behind the dark glasses. Seven minutes. We need to thrash this in four, five to seven minutes. Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I think I can be very quick here, Your Honour. We are proposing to call evidence on Thursday. We would like the indulgence of the Trial Chamber as follows: We hope that hope that four of the five witnesses we wish to call are going to arrive within the next 24 hours. We would tend to try and call two on Thursday and two on Friday. The other witness can't be here until Monday. Perhaps we could collectively review the position, as far as he's concerned, later in the week, but at the moment, what we are asking is your permission to call two on Thursday and two on Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, we need a list of who those are and whatever statements they have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: -- and exhibits and all of that, if it's going to be that quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, and you have to identify which two will come on Wednesday and which two will come on Friday. We know who the other one is.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: That's completely reasonable, of course, Your Honours, we will do that, and parties to the case will get some form of proofing note when they have been properly proofed, but time is not really so our side, and we will do our best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can we know now, if you know? I mean, surely you've got to know what their order is.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: We don't know what their order is. I could tell my learned friend who the fifth witness is, the one who can't be here. I will do that immediately after the Court has risen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we know that, too. We know who the fifth one is, I would imagine?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: No, Your Honours I don't think are aware of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. No problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Let's proceed along the lines that -- but, please, you have a responsibility to disclose to your colleagues and Mr. McCloskey the order of ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I think Mr. Krgovic, who is responsible for this aspect of the case, will make that decision tomorrow early on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, you have to make it today not tomorrow. We've had loud protests from this side of the courtroom when there was a delay of even a few hours in disclosing the order of -- this is not in accordance with what the practice that we have adopted in the past. So please, Mr. Krgovic, make your decision and communicate to the Prosecution the name of the first two witnesses you intend to produce.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have a problem. A witness who needs to testify has been removed from a truck in Germany on his trip from Turkey, and he's due to arrive this evening. The other witness is awaiting permission from the National Council for Cooperation with the Tribunal because he's in active service. And we're waiting for these documents today, and that is why we are unable to tell you until we meet them. They still haven't arrived in The Hague, and according to the information I have, they are due to arrive this evening about 7.00 p.m. via Prague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But that doesn't -- shouldn't be an obstacle in identifying who will testify on Thursday. It may be a logistical problem in having them arrive in time, but it shouldn't be an obstacle identifying any of them. And what about the other two?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Your Honour, we will provide an order after court -- after we've had a consultation sometime this afternoon --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: -- based on best plans; that is, everyone being here and everything being in order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Of course, if there are any changes, we will let my learned friend know. But we will try and stick to what we say this afternoon, if at all possible. We give that guarantee.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Documents? You have a list of documents Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The list is around -- it's four new ones, 1999, 4550, 4568, 4574.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any objections, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: None, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. These are all the admitted. You had no documents that you made use of. So I think we can adjourn until Thursday. Is it in the morning or the afternoon? Thursday in the afternoon at 2.15 p.m. All right. And my thanks to the staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
